sql-schema.note: The schema is Prisma's own schema language, and `prisma migrate dev --schema schema.sql` rejects SQL as invalid schema lines.

views.note: With the `views` preview feature, `prisma db pull` writes the view, but `prisma migrate dev --create-only` writes an empty migration for a changed query.

functions-triggers.note: Prisma's schema cannot declare a function or trigger: `prisma db pull` leaves both out, and `prisma migrate dev --create-only` writes an empty migration.

rls.note: Prisma's schema cannot declare a policy: `prisma db pull` warns that row level security is not supported, and `prisma migrate dev --create-only` writes an empty migration.

renames.note: `prisma migrate dev` warns that the column's values will be lost and, once confirmed, writes a drop and an add, so `prisma migrate deploy` empties the column.

view-dependencies.note: `prisma migrate dev --create-only` writes a bare `set data type`, which `prisma migrate deploy` cannot run while a view reads the column.

non-blocking.note: `prisma migrate dev --create-only` writes a plain `create index`, and `@@index` takes no `concurrently` argument.

drift.note: `prisma migrate deploy` ran the pending migration on a database with a hand-added column without a word, and `prisma migrate status` listed only the pending migration.

out-of-order.note: `prisma migrate deploy` ran a merged migration that sorts before one already run without a word.

branch-switch.note: After a switch, `prisma migrate dev` reported the other branch's migration as drift and stopped, saying the whole `public` schema must be reset and all its data lost.

lockfile.note: `migration_lock.toml` holds only the database provider, so two branches' migrations merged in git without a conflict.

sql-schema.note: The schema is TypeScript: `drizzle-kit generate` finds no schema in a `.sql` file.

functions-triggers.note: Drizzle's schema cannot declare a trigger or a trigger function: `drizzle-kit pull` leaves both out, and `drizzle-kit generate` finds no changes.

data-loss.note: `drizzle-kit push` asks to confirm the lost data, but `drizzle-kit generate` writes the drop without asking and `drizzle-kit migrate` runs it.

view-dependencies.note: `drizzle-kit generate` writes a bare `set data type`, which fails while a view reads the column.

non-blocking.note: `drizzle-kit generate` writes a plain `create index`, and Drizzle 1.0's index builder has no `.concurrently()`.

shadow.note: `drizzle-kit generate` writes the migration from snapshots without opening a database, and `drizzle-kit migrate` runs it straight on the target.

drift.note: `drizzle-kit migrate` ran the pending migration on a database with a hand-added column without a word.

out-of-order.note: `drizzle-kit migrate` ran a merged migration that sorts before one already run without a word, even when the two migrations end in different schemas in each order.

branch-switch.note: `drizzle-kit migrate` left the other branch's table in place unmentioned, and after `drizzle-kit push` removed it, `drizzle-kit migrate` failed with "relation already exists".

lockfile.note: Each `drizzle-kit generate` writes its own folder, so two branches' migrations merged in git without a conflict.

views.note: Atlas Pro only: the free standard build refuses views until `atlas login`, and the community build ignores the change.

functions-triggers.note: Atlas Pro only: the free standard build refuses functions until `atlas login`, and the community build ignores the change.

rls.note: Atlas Pro only: the free standard build refuses policies until `atlas login`, and the community build ignores the change.

data-loss.note: `atlas migrate diff` writes the drop and `atlas migrate apply` runs it without asking; `atlas schema apply` asks to approve every plan alike.

view-dependencies.note: Atlas Pro only: the free standard build refuses the view until `atlas login`, and the community build's `alter column type` fails on it.

non-blocking.note: Only with `concurrent_index` turned on in `atlas.hcl`; by default `atlas schema apply` writes a plain `create index`.

drift.note: Atlas Pro only: the free builds' `atlas migrate apply` ran the pending migration on a database with a hand-added column without a word.

branch-switch.note: `atlas migrate apply` refused this branch's migration as out of order, or ran it beside the other branch's table, and the community build has no `atlas migrate down`.

open-source.note: The Apache-2.0 community build leaves `atlas migrate down` to the standard build, under Ariga's EULA, and drift alerts to Atlas Pro.

non-blocking.note: `pgdelta schema apply` writes a plain `create index`, even for an index declared `concurrently`.

drift.note: `pgdelta apply` refuses a plan whose database changed by hand since it was planned, but it keeps no migration history to deploy.

out-of-order.note: It plans changes only, and keeps no migration history.

branch-switch.note: `pgdelta schema apply` takes the database to this branch's schema and keeps the rest, but it keeps no migrations to rewind.

lockfile.note: It plans changes only, and keeps no migration history.

sql-schema.note: `liquibase diff-changelog` compares two live databases, so the target schema has to be built into a second database first.

views.note: On MySQL, `liquibase diff-changelog` copies the view's query with the reference database's name in it, so the view reads the wrong database unless both share a name.

functions-triggers.note: `liquibase diff-changelog` writes nothing for a changed function or trigger, and refuses `--diff-types=functions,triggers` as unknown types.

rls.note: `liquibase diff-changelog` writes nothing for a changed policy, and refuses `--diff-types=policies` as an unknown type.

renames.note: `liquibase diff-changelog` writes an `addColumn` and a `dropColumn`, and `liquibase update` loses the column's rows.

data-loss.note: `liquibase diff-changelog` writes the `dropColumn`, and `liquibase update` runs it without asking.

view-dependencies.note: `liquibase diff-changelog` writes a bare `modifyDataType`, which `liquibase update` cannot run while a view reads the column.

shadow.note: `liquibase update` runs the changelog straight on the target, and no command tries it on a throwaway database first.

drift.note: `liquibase update` ran the pending changeset on a database with a hand-added column without a word.

out-of-order.note: `liquibase update` ran a changeset that sorts before ones already run without a word.

branch-switch.note: `liquibase update` ran this branch's changeset and left the other branch's table in place unmentioned.

open-source.note: Liquibase 5.0.4 ships under the Functional Source License (FSL-1.1-ALv2), which isn't OSI-approved.

shadow.note: Flyway Enterprise only: Community refuses `flyway diff` with a shadow build environment, and `flyway migrate` runs straight on the target.

drift.note: Flyway Enterprise only: Community refuses `flyway check -drift`, and `flyway migrate` ran the pending migration on a database with a hand-added column without a word.

branch-switch.note: `flyway migrate` refused with a checksum mismatch on the other branch's migration, leaving its table in place, and `flyway undo` needs a Redgate edition.

lockfile.note: Two branches' `V2__…` files merged in git without a conflict, and `flyway migrate` then refused with "Found more than one migration with version 2".

open-source.note: The Apache-2.0 OSS edition has no `diff`, `check` or `undo`, which are in Redgate's editions under its EULA.
